brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Concept of spatial proximity-based file organization is a genuinely interesting departure from list/grid paradigms
Empty rounded zones in the canvas suggest topic clusters, hinting at a meaningful spatial language
Color-coded document chips provide a fast visual identity per file type or topic
dominant_weaknesses: Document tiles are catastrophically overlapped in the top-left, making labels unreadable and destroying the proximity metaphor
Massive empty canvas zones with only four undefined blobs feel unfinished, with no labels, axes, or topic anchors
Typography is cramped, inconsistent in wrap, and labels collide; file size metadata adds noise without hierarchy
fix_priorities: Decluster the top-left pile — distribute documents across the canvas with breathing room and clear proximity relationships
Label the four cluster zones (topics/projects) so spatial meaning becomes legible
Establish typographic hierarchy: title prominent, metadata muted, consistent tile sizing
Refine palette so chip colors map to a coherent topic taxonomy rather than arbitrary hues
rationale.norman_balance: Weak across all three layers — visceral is muddled by overlap, behavioral is broken by unreadable clustering, reflective concept is intriguing but unrealized.
rationale.intent_fit: The spatial-canvas intent is conceptually present but executionally collapsed — files pile in one corner instead of meaningfully occupying topic space.
